findings.description: The city published a complete-application notice, with a mid-June decision deadline, for Prologis and Caltrain's master-planned redevelopment of the 4th and King railyards into up to 8 million square feet (roughly 4 million of offices, ~2,500 housing units) anchored by an 850-foot tower and a modernized Caltrain station, coordinated with the Portal Project's downtown extension.

extra.proposed_stories_note: no single street address given; the site spans the railyard blocks between 4th and 7th Streets

citation.label: San Francisco YIMBY, “Approval Deadline Set For Caltrain Railyards Mega-Project, San Francisco,” 24 April 2026

resolution.note: No usable address. The article names the site only by its cross streets and the station it redevelops -- "4th and King", "the blocks at 4th Street and 7th Street" -- and never prints a street number for the parcel; inventing one (e.g. the depot's own 700 4th Street) would not be a fact the article states. Worth a second look if a later filing prints an address for the phase-one parcel.

publish.note: Declined for lack of a usable address; see resolution note. The project itself is real and well documented elsewhere (Prologis/Caltrain press materials), but this pipeline publishes only what a story states plainly about a specific parcel.

findings.description: SF Recreation and Parks Department filed plans to reconfigure Crocker Amazon Park's ballfields at Moscow Street and Geneva Avenue from five fields to six (three youth, three adult), most with synthetic turf and lighting, plus new pathways, gardens, a plaza and dog parks. Verde Design is the landscape architect.

citation.label: San Francisco YIMBY, “Permits Filed for Community Baseball Field Renovation in San Francisco,” 22 April 2026

resolution.note: Not a building. Crocker Amazon Park's ballfields are park land, not a structure with a parcel this site documents as a building; the root AGENTS.md scope is the built environment, one page per building.
